summary: Friedrich Bechtel was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick (~1873–1876). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1878–1895) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1895–1924).

Friedrich Bollensen studied theology and Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1834). An Indologist and linguist, he held posts at Gatchina Orphanage (1834), Saint Petersburg State University (~1845–1856), the Main Pedagogical Institute (1846), and Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

Friedrich Haag worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler (~1865–1869, 1873), Göttingen (~1869–1870), and Berlin (~1870–1871). He served as Dozent at the University of Zurich (1873–1884) and professor at the University of Bern (~1878–1914).

Friedrich Hirth was a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University (~1865–1867), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1867–1868), and the University of Greifswald (~1868–1869), later holding a post at Columbia University (~1902–1917).

Friedrich Max Müller was an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, Paris, and under scholars including Brockhaus, Burnouf, Bopp, Schelling, and Wilson. He held posts at Oxford (1850, 1854, 1883–1900) and All Souls College (~1858–1900).

Friedrich Müller worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Theresianum, University of Vienna (under Anton Boller ~1853–1855), and Göttingen (~1855–1857). He held posts at the Austrian National Library (1861–1866) and the University of Vienna (from 1866; professor 1869).

Friedrich Rückert worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Würzburg (~1805–1808), Heidelberg (~1809–1810), and under Franz Bopp (~1818–1819), holding professorships at Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1841–1849).

Friedrich Schlegel studied at Göttingen, Leipzig, and in Paris under Alexander Hamilton (1802–1804) and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (~1803–1804). Active in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, he held posts at TU Dresden, the University of Jena (~1800–1801), and the University of Cologne (~1804–1808).
Friedrich Weller was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist who studied under August Conrady (~1908–1915). In 1928, he was appointed Ordinarius for Indology at Leipzig University.

Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph von Schelling was a philosopher who studied at the Tübinger Stift, University of Tübingen (~1790–1795), and Leipzig University (~1796–1798). He held professorships at Jena (1798), Würzburg (~1803–1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1820–1827), Munich (~1827–1841), and Berlin (~1841–1846).

Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl worked in linguistics. He studied at Leipzig University (~1825–1826) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1826–1829), later holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1829–1833), Breslau (~1833–1839), Bonn (~1839–1865), and Leipzig (~1865–1875).

Friedrich Windischmann was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Munich (~1827–1832) and Bonn under Christian Lassen (~1832–1833). He held posts at Munich (~1836–1848) and the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising (~1848–1861).
Friedrich Zarncke was a linguistics scholar who studied at Leipzig University (~1844–1847). He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1850–1852) and Leipzig University (~1852–1891).

Friedrich von Spiegel worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, Hermann Brockhaus, and Christian Lassen at the University of Bonn, and later held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1849–1890).

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics, studying at the University of Amsterdam, Banaras Hindu University, and VU Amsterdam. He held posts at VU Amsterdam, the University of Amsterdam (1962–1967), MIT (~1967–1968), and UC Berkeley (~1968–1991).
Fritz Johaentgen was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (1919–1923). He later held academic posts at Munich (~1934–1941) and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1946–1969).

Fujio Taniguchi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa, among other teachers. He held a post as lecturer at Chiba College of Health Science (attested 1991).

Fumihiko Sueki studied at the University of Tokyo (~1973–1979) in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1988–2003; emeritus ~2009), the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (~2009–2014), and SOKENDAI (~2009–2014).

Fumimaro Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1953–1957). He held posts at Ryukoku University, Hanazono University, Nagoya University, and Aichi Gakuin University.
